claims.text: As-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder has a heterogeneous microstructure characteristic of rapid solidification.
A secondary laser scan reheating each deposited layer to 300–400 °C for 1–2 seconds can induce partial recrystallization in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed secondary scan will provide effective stress relief in AlCrFeNiSi.
The secondary annealing pass should be applied immediately after every LPBF layer and monitored to maintain 300–400 °C for 1–2 seconds.
Miniature components with characteristic dimensions of 0.5–2 mm can be processed using this intervention under inert atmosphere and 100–150 °C build-plate preheat.
Uniform application of the secondary scan after every layer will avoid over-aging and maintain microstructural integrity.
Short-duration, moderate-temperature annealing will produce stress relaxation and partial recrystallization with limited grain growth.
The annealing treatment will refine grain boundaries.
Recovery and partial recrystallization immediately after solidification will enable lattice relaxation at grain boundaries and thereby relieve thermal-mismatch stresses.
The short annealing treatment will preserve the fine-grained microstructure needed for mechanical performance.
Relative to high-thermal-load LPBF without the secondary scan, treated components will have significantly lower residual stress.
The treated components will have improved ductility relative to the baseline.
The treated components will have improved fatigue resistance relative to the baseline.
The treated components will have a more uniform microstructure and fewer process-induced defects than the baseline.
The intervention is expected to be effective specifically for 0.5–2 mm AlCrFeNiSi components made with 100–150 °C preheat under inert LPBF conditions.
Inadequate temperature control may cause grain coarsening that compromises mechanical integrity.
KAM mapping can be used as an indicator of local lattice distortion and residual plastic strain when assessing stress relief.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant residual-stress reduction exceeding 20% together with failure to improve mechanical performance, or observation of mechanically harmful excessive grain growth, will falsify the hypothesis.
